title: Data-residency-aware-audit-tokenization-and-rbac-reconciliation-playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This playbook describes Redwood’s standard process for tokenizing audit events to meet cross-border data residency requirements while preserving RBAC reconciliation and forensic fidelity. It balances three objectives: (1) ensure audit evidence meets legal/regulatory locality/residency constraints, (2) maintain proof of authorization decisions for incident investigations, and (3) minimize leakage of sensitive PII or customer data into long-term, cross-region stores.

Scope:
- Applies to: Redwood-Audit service (internal event pipeline), Redwood-Authz (authorization decisions), Redwood-LogStore (hot storage), and Redwood-Evidence (immutable packaging).
- Regions: Global (us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Not in scope: application-level telemetry (handled by app teams), third-party SaaS logs unless ingested into Redwood-Audit.

Definitions:
- Tokenization: Deterministic replacement of sensitive values (user identifiers, resource IDs) with reversible tokens backed by KMS-wrapped key material and per-region envelopes.
- RBAC reconciliation: Re-running authorization checks against recorded inputs to confirm the decision path (roles, attributes, policies) that led to a granted/denied action.
- Evidence bundle: An immutable zip of raw and tokenized events, policy snapshots, and the KMS unwrapping request log used for audits or legal holds.

Principles:
1) Residency-first: Raw PII or residency-sensitive fields are never replicated outside the legal residency boundary unless explicitly approved via an evidence escrow request.
2) Reconstructability: Tokenization must be reversible for authorized auditors when a legal/process-approved unseal is performed; reversible operations are auditable and time-limited.
3) Minimal exposure: Tokenized fields are usable for RBAC reconciliation (same-value mapping) without exposing original values in cross-region analytics.
4) Separation of duties: Key custodianship, evidence approval, and forensic analysis are different roles/team assignments with enforced approvals.

Architecture (text diagram):
- Redwood services: app -> Redwood-Audit (collector) -> per-region Tokenizer -> Redwood-LogStore (hot, region-local) -> Replication/Retention policy -> Redwood-Evidence (immutable packaging)
- Key management: Region KMS (cms-redwood-audit-%REGION%); token envelope keys stored in KMS; unwrap operations logged to Audit-KMS-Events stream.

Playbook: Tokenization & RBAC reconciliation flow

1) Pre-deployment configuration (owner: Security & Infra)
   1.1 Create tokenization profile per workload. Fields: field_name, sensitivity_level, token_type (deterministic/reversible/one-way), residency_scope (region codes), retention_window_days.
   1.2 Approve KMS keys: deploy kms keys named cms-redwood-audit-us-west-2, cms-redwood-audit-eu-central-1, etc. Ensure CMK rotation cadence = 365d and that keys have key policy restricting decrypt to keys/unseal service principals.
   1.3 Register the profile in Redwood-Audit config-store with labels: workload, team, data_classification.

2) Runtime event processing (owner: Audit Engineering)
   2.1 Collector receives event JSON. Example event:

       {
         "ts": "2026-02-10T12:23:44Z",
         "actor_id": "u-1234567890",
         "resource_id": "res-aws-prod-42",
         "action": "model.deploy",
         "decision": "allow",
         "decision_context": {"roles": ["platform-admin"], "attrs": { "team": "infra" }}
       }

   2.2 Tokenizer applies per-field rules:
       - actor_id -> deterministic reversible token using region envelope: token = TK_det(regional_key, actor_id) e.g. TKN:r1:8f3a...
       - resource_id -> one-way SHA256 prefix + short token for indexing: idx_res = SHA256(res_id)[:12]
       - decision_context.roles -> kept in plain (non-PII)
   2.3 Tokenized event stored in Redwood-LogStore in the same region as the originating event. Unencrypted fields are indexed for queries; token fields are stored but not searchable by plaintext unless unwrapped at time of authorized forensic retrieval.

3) RBAC reconciliation mode (owner: Authz & Security)
   3.1 Use case: customer reports unauthorized access; SRE triggers RBAC-recon request.
   3.2 Procedure:
       - Step A: Investigator files Evidence Unseal Request (see Appendix B) with business justification and legal approval. Request populates evidence ticket in Redwood-Evidence: ticket_id, scope, region, start_ts, end_ts, approver_id.
       - Step B: Conditional KMS unwrap: evidence-ops service uses requester principal to request ephemeral unwrap tokens from regional KMS. Each unwrap request is recorded in KMS-Events stream.
       - Step C: Reconstruct decision inputs: for each tokenized event, perform mapping: original_actor = TK_rev(region_key, token) and feed original_actor and original resource ID (if reversible) into Redwood-Authz simulation engine to recompute decision path.
       - Step D: Produce reconciliation report: show policy version, role bindings snapshot, attribute values, decision delta (match/mismatch).

4) Forensic retrieval & evidence packaging (owner: Security)
   4.1 Packaging rules:
       - Evidence bundles must include: raw tokenized events (region-local), KMS unwrap audit entries, policy snapshots (versions), role binding snapshots, and a signed manifest (SHA256).
       - For cross-border transfer of reconstructed PII, produce a limited-scope evidence escrow: time-limited zip encrypted with requester’s ephemeral RSA public key and approved by Legal.
   4.2 Retention policy table (example):

       | Object                    | Region storage | Retention | Residency note |
       |---------------------------|----------------|-----------|----------------|
       | Tokenized audit events    | region-local   | 365d      | never copied outside region without escrow |
       | KMS unwrap logs           | central-locked | 1095d     | metadata only replicated (no plaintext) |
       | Evidence bundles (sealed) | region-local   | 1825d     | escrowed copies require Legal + CISO |

5) Emergency unseal / incident acceleration (owner: Incident Response + CISO)
   5.1 Criteria: active breach impacting customer data, law enforcement request with valid warrant, or cross-region incident containment where live attributes needed.
   5.2 Emergency steps:
       - Triage call with CISO, Legal, IR lead, and KMS custodian.
       - Obtain emergency authorization token via multi-party vault (2-of-3 approvals).
       - Log emergency unwrap event with high-priority tag and forward to Evidence queue for expedited packaging.
       - Post-incident: Produce full audit of unseal operations within 72 hours and publish to internal compliance portal.

6) Automation & SLOs (owner: Platform Reliability)
   - Tokenization latency: 99th percentile <= 35ms per event for steady-state ingest.
   - Evidence package creation time (standard): 95% within 6 hours for scoped time ranges up to 7 days.
   - Emergency unseal acknowledgment: < 30 minutes for approval workflow (operations target).

7) Roles & responsibilities:
   - Security: owns policy, approves tokenization profiles, reviews unseal requests.
   - Audit Engineering: implements tokenizer, maintains per-region KMS bindings.
   - Authz Team: maintains simulation engine; owns RBAC reconciliation test harness.
   - Legal & Compliance: approves escrow and cross-border transfers; maintains legal hold matrix.
   - Evidence Ops: assembles sealed bundles and maintains chain-of-custody.

8) Checklist: Pre-request validation (for Evidence requests)
   - [ ] Ticket created with clear scope and timestamps.
   - [ ] Legal approval attached if cross-region or contains customer PII.
   - [ ] CISO or designated deputy sign-off for emergency unseal.
   - [ ] KMS custodian notified and available for unwrap coordination.

Appendix A — Example tokenization profile (YAML)

profile_name: model-control-audit
fields:
  - name: actor_id
    sensitivity: high
    token_type: reversible-deterministic
    residency: [us-west-2, eu-central-1]
  - name: resource_id
    sensitivity: medium
    token_type: one-way-hash
    residency: [us-west-2]
retention_days: 365
owner: infra-security

Appendix B — Evidence Unseal Request CLI example

# create request (investigator)
redwood-evidence request create --ticket "INC-2026-0123" --region eu-central-1 --start 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-02-02T00:00:00Z --reason "suspected unauthorized role escalation"

# attach legal approval (Legal)
redwood-evidence request approve --id REQ-2026-778 --approver "legal@redwood.com" --note "warrant-12345"

# evidence ops assemble (ops)
redwood-evidence assemble --id REQ-2026-778 --out /tmp/evidence-REQ-2026-778.zip

Audit signals to surface in the console for reviewers:
- KMS unwrap events (principal, key_id, timestamp, justification ticket_id)
- Evidence bundle manifest checksums and signer
- RBAC reconciliation outcomes (match/mismatch with policy version)
- Unusual pattern detection: repeated unwraps, excessive partial unseals, cross-region export attempts

Governance & review cadence:
- Quarterly review of tokenization profiles (owner: Security).
- Annual tabletop for emergency unseal procedures with Legal, CISO, and Evidence Ops.
